I will keep my planting simple and familiar because I am 74, and I want steady income with work I can still manage. In Quzhou County, the wheat-maize rotation fits my land, local weather, and irrigation conditions best, so I will stay with that as my main pattern. I will plant winter wheat on all my land first, then follow with summer maize after wheat harvest. I would choose improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easier to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better. I will not make the plan too complicated with many cash crops, because that increases labor, management pressure, and risk. I would use moderate fertilizer instead of pushing too hard, because I want stable production and I do not want to waste money or damage the soil. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing, and it works well enough for my usual rotation. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat here depends more on timely watering, especially for overwintering, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray only as much as needed to control the common diseases, weeds, and insects, because clean fields matter but I do not want unnecessary cost.
